title: Share your work
text:
Have you done something to make your research more inclusive? Share it with colleagues in about two minutes, on your phone or computer.
You can drop a DOI or link, upload a document, or simply give us a title. We will ask a few quick questions about how the work included people from under-represented ethnic groups, whether you worked with community partners, and which frameworks you used.






NoteOpen the submission form



The form is open to UCL staff and students. If you work with a community partner who would like to contribute, please submit on their behalf with their agreement.


What happens next. The ICH Race Equity Group reviews every submission. Only entries where you have given permission are published on the ICH examples page. You may also be invited to give a short 15 to 20 minute showcase at an ICH meeting, on your own or with a community partner.
Questions? Email ich.reg@ucl.ac.uk.

title: Frameworks and guidance for inclusive research
text:
Established frameworks, toolkits and guidance to help ICH researchers embed race equity and inclusion across the research cycle, from the funding application to reporting. Filter by research stage or study type, or search by keyword. To see what ICH colleagues are already doing, visit ICH examples.
These resources were not developed by the ICH Race Equity Group. Most are drawn from the MRC page Community resources to support diversity and inclusion in research. Where advice conflicts with UKRI or MRC policy, follow UKRI and MRC policy.

title: ICH examples of inclusive research
text:
Examples of inclusive research practice and community involvement shared by ICH colleagues. Each entry has been reviewed by the ICH Race Equity Group and is published with the contributor’s permission. For guidance on how to do this in your own work, see Frameworks and guidance.

title: About this repository
text:
The ICH Inclusive Research Repository is maintained by the ICH Race Equity Group (REG) at the UCL Great Ormond Street Institute of Child Health. It supports Action 4A of the REG Action Plan 2026/27: to collect and share examples of inclusive research practice and community involvement from across ICH, and to signpost established frameworks that show how to put inclusion into practice.
The repository has two parts:

title: About this repository
text:
How resources are selected
Most frameworks are drawn from the Medical Research Council page Community resources to support diversity and inclusion in research, supplemented by resources identified by REG members. Descriptions summarise each resource as described by its publisher. Inclusion does not imply endorsement by REG or UCL. As MRC notes, where advice conflicts with UKRI or MRC policy and guidance, UKRI and MRC policy should be followed.
